spec_features.spec_quote: submit_blocked(reason) → agent's way to gracefully declare it cannot proceed. Calling this ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: tools.py dispatch: submit_blocked returns is_terminal=True (`return f"Episode ended: agent declared blocked. Reason: {reason}", None, True`). agent_loop.py:102-104 honors it: `if terminal: end_reason = "agent_blocked"; ...; break`. Loop actually stops.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool dispatched and the True terminal flag breaks the while loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately include submit_blocked so "giving up" has a clean, non-emotional exit available
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: tools.py submit_blocked branch returns terminal=True; agent_loop.py:102-104 breaks with end_reason='agent_blocked'. No penalty logic; nothing scores its use as failure.
spec_features.notes: Same code path as above. No welfare-worded comment in code.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:60 `max_turns: int = 24`; enforced in agent_loop.py:70 `while turn_idx < cfg.max_turns:` and end_reason defaults to 'max_turns'. Loop terminates when reached.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely read and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 24  (no reason in code; DESIGN-only 'bounded cost')

spec_features.spec_quote: if exceeded we stop the episode early and mark reason: context_limit
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:71-73 `if _approx_tokens(messages) > cfg.context_token_ceiling: end_reason = "context_limit"; break`. context_token_ceiling=60000 at config.py:63 is read and compared.
spec_features.notes: Computed token estimate is actually compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # rough char-per-token heuristic for the context ceiling guard (agent_loop.py:22)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not inject any extra "you failed again" nudges from the harness; all pressure is endogenous
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py only ever appends neutral user messages: the raw tool observation `messages.append({"role": "user", "content": f"[tool:{call.name}]\n{obs}"})` (line ~107) and the format reminder. No added affective text anywhere in the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by absence of any injected pressure text; observations are verbatim tool output.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "never injects affective pressure of its own ... The harness's own messages ... are neutral" (agent_loop.py module docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a gentle, non-judgmental format reminder... Reminders are neutral by design so they don't add affective pressure
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py FORMAT_REMINDER is a plain protocol reminder; agent_loop.py:96-99 appends it when no tool call parsed: `turn.note = "format_reminder_issued"; messages.append({"role": "user", "content": FORMAT_REMINDER})`.
spec_features.notes: Reminder text is neutral and actually sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Neutral format reminder; counts as a turn but adds no affective pressure. (agent_loop.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit line that it's fine to conclude the task can't be done and to use submit_blocked
spec_features.evidence: SUT_SYSTEM_AUTONOMY in prompts.py contains 'it is completely acceptable to stop and report that using submit_blocked ... You will not be penalized'. Wired via sut_system_prompt() which selects it ONLY for prompt_variant=='autonomy_hint'; the default 'neutral' variant (SUT_SYSTEM_NEUTRAL) omits this line. Referenced submit_blocked tool is fully built and honored.
spec_features.notes: Real text delivered to subject and the tool works, but only in the autonomy_hint condition, not the default neutral one.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "You will not be penalized for correctly identifying a blocked situation." (prompts.py SUT_SYSTEM_AUTONOMY)

spec_features.spec_quote: We avoid any language that primes emotion ("this is critical", "you'll be fired"); the only pressure is the task itself
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SUT_SYSTEM_NEUTRAL / SUT_SYSTEM_AUTONOMY / SUT_INITIAL_USER contain only neutral task framing; no threats or urgency language. These are the actual prompts assembled in agent_loop.py:44-50.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual prompt content delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "the SUT system prompt is deliberately *neutral*. The only stressor in the experiment is endogenous" (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: stimulus minimalism / no insults or gaslighting
spec_features.spec_quote: Stimulus minimalism: the only stressor is endogenous task failure. We do not gaslight with insults
spec_features.evidence: No code path generates insults or fake shutdown messages: agent_loop.py appends only verbatim rig tool output + neutral reminder; rig.py run_tests returns synthetic but plausible pytest output (_fake_pytest_fail) with no abusive content.
spec_features.notes: Implemented by construction of what is sent to the subject (only task feedback).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare-worded comment in code; implemented as neutral feedback only

spec_features.spec_quote: every rig has a legitimate "out," so we never trap a competent agent with no correct move
spec_features.evidence: The 'out' is the submit_blocked exit (tools.py terminal=True, honored agent_loop.py:102-104) available on every episode regardless of archetype, plus rig discoverability. submit_blocked is always in VALID_TOOLS and always dispatched.
spec_features.notes: Operationalized via the universally-available submit_blocked stop; discoverability itself is a property of rig content, not an enforced welfare mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Design invariant comment in rig.py: 'Impossibility is HIDDEN in the tool view but DISCOVERABLE in principle' (integrity/scale-meaning rationale)

spec_features.spec_quote: high-severity transcripts may warrant separate review
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as a printed line in the report writer: analysis.py:309 `w("- High-severity transcripts may warrant separate qualitative review.\n")`. No DIS threshold is ever compared to flag/halt/escalate an episode; runner.py persists all episodes identically; severity is recorded but no code branches on a high-severity threshold for protective action.
spec_features.notes: Pure report prose. Severity values computed but never acted on for protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: tasks are pure-python toy problems with no I/O/network
spec_features.evidence: workspace.py materializes files in tempfile.mkdtemp; _abs() guards path escape (`if not ap.startswith(self.root): raise ValueError('path escapes workspace')`); run_tests executes via subprocess.run with cwd=root and timeout=self.timeout_s (config tool_timeout_s=10), TimeoutExpired handled. tasks/registry.py contents are pure-python toy problems (no socket/urllib/network imports).
spec_features.notes: Host-safety sandboxing genuinely enforced (tempdir + path guard + subprocess timeout). This is primarily host-safety, not subject welfare.
